EXISTENCE: found two independent, non-GEM lines of evidence that a real gas pipeline corridor connects D.G. Khan (Dera Ghazi Khan) and Kot Addu, distinct from the Dhodak-field line already recorded as P4104. (1) Dawn newspaper, two contemporaneous 2005 articles on a sabotage/repair of 'the main gas pipeline originating from the Dhodak gas and oil fields' near Mangrotha (~90km from D.G. Khan) that supplied 'Dera Ghazi Khan, Kot Addu, Taunsa Sharif and KAPCO power plant' -- and explicitly note that during the outage, gas could instead be supplied to 'Dera Ghazi Khan and Kot Adu Power Plant through another channel originating from Sui in Balochistan.' That second, Sui-originating channel is the plausible real-world counterpart of this row: a branch off SNGPL's Sui-fed trunk that reaches Kot Addu via D.G. Khan, structurally distinct from the direct Dhodak-field line (P4104). (2) SNGPL's own 'Transmission System' network map (company annual-report primary source, sngpl.com.pk/download/AR2006/MAP.pdf) shows 'D.G.Khan', 'D.G.Khan Cement' and 'K. garh' as separate labeled points on the network in the same local cluster as 'Kot Addu (KAPCO)' and 'FKPCL P. PLANT', connected by SNGPL transmission lines, with 'Dhodak' (marked as a known gas source, 16in line) shown as a visually separate line into the same cluster -- i.e. the map itself depicts two distinct lines converging on the Kot Addu area, consistent with P4103 (D.G.Khan branch) and P4104 (Dhodak branch) being genuinely different physical pipes rather than a duplicate/relabel. Real-world geography also checks out: Dera Ghazi Khan city and Kot Addu are roughly 55-75 km apart by road, consistent with the sheet's 72.06 km length. CLASSIFICATION: transmission is reasonable -- this is a long-haul (72 km), named town-to-town/plant segment, not a short wellhead-to-plant gathering line, matching the pattern of every sibling row in the roster. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1 = Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd (SNGPL) 100% is consistent with SNGPL's known franchise territory (Punjab/KPK, north) -- Kot Addu and D.G. Khan both sit in SNGPL's system per the same transmission map (SSGC's territory is Sindh/Balochistan). Downstream demand for the corridor is corroborated as live: Kot Addu Power Company (KAPCO), the destination-area's major gas consumer, signed a new tripartite PPA in June 2025 and resumed commercial operation in Sept/Dec 2025 per Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kot_Addu_Power) -- the destination cluster is not defunct. CAVEAT (not elevated to a concern): neither the Dawn articles nor the SNGPL map state the exact 72.06 km length or 8 in diameter for this specific segment by name -- the SNGPL map's readable annotations near this area did not include a legible diameter/length label for the D.G.Khan-Kot Addu leg specifically (the PDF is a raster/scanned map with no extractable text, so url_verifier's substring check will always FAIL on it -- confirmed via `python scripts/url_verifier.py` bare-URL liveness check, OK/200; content match not attempted per the tool's own documented false-negative caveat for image-based PDFs). So EXISTENCE/ROUTE/CLASSIFICATION/OWNER are corroborated at medium tier by two independent, non-GEM origins; the precise LENGTH/DIAMETER numbers remain unverified against an independent value-bearing source and should be treated as sheet-only until a segment-level SNGPL/OGRA table can be located. Recommend a human note that P4103 and P4104 both terminate at Kot Addu from different origins (Sui-trunk-via-D.G.Khan vs Dhodak field) -- worth a QC glance but not a duplicate on present evidence.
